Header: Nilaparvata lugens เพลี้ยกระโดดสีน้ำตาล

Prevention: Use appropriate planting date: avoid planting during
RD29, RD31, RD41, RD47, RD49, PSL2, SPR1, SPR2, SPR90).
Avoid continuous cropping (allow fallow period), and don’t plant the same variety in large area (plant more than 2 varieties with same harvesting days)
Preferred planting method: transplanting by hand or machine, or parachuting
If direct seeding use sowing rate of 15-20 kg/ rai
Crop rotation (with mungbean, vegetables, or peanut)
Plant yellow or white flowering plants on the bund (to increase diversity for natural enemies such as mirid bug)
Monitoring: Start surveying field 2 times per month 15
DAS or counting in the field 15
DAS) look at stem above water level).
BPH at lights along the road or at home
Observe natural enemies (mirid bug, spider, lady beetle, rove beetle, long- horned grasshoppers, ground beetles, damselfly, dragonfly)
Direct Control: Trapping: use giant light trap (sucking machine) for long- wing
BPH in seedling and pre- harvesting stage
Botanical control: neem extract (most effective during nymph stage)
If >70% of crop damage plough soil up and over, and replant (wait 1 month to start new crop)
In irrigated areas, drain water to create unsuitable environment for
BPH and encourage ants to come in and eat the nymphs
Restrictions: RD recommendations for insecticide dosage, application method and crop stages
Don’t use 36 prohibited resurgence insecticide on
DAS, IRAC group 16, WHO III Buprofezin + Isoprocarb 40-60
